title: Modelling Load Imbalance In Shared Memory Multicore Systems
problem: Memory bandwidth saturates with increasing core count; mainstream performance models assume homogeneous per-core memory traffic, leading to inaccurate time estimates when traffic is inhomogeneous
motivation: Develop more accurate performance models for memory-bandwidth-limited workloads on shared memory multicores with non-uniform per-core memory access patterns
method: The model predicts execution time by accounting for the fact that different cores access shared memory at unequal rates (per-core traffic inhomogeneity)—a reality that traditional models ignore by assuming uniform traffic. It uses three hardware parameters to calculate how cores compete for limited memory bandwidth when access patterns are unbalanced. This approach produces accurate time predictions even when cores have very different memory demands, whereas bandwidth-based models with their uniform-traffic assumption fail in these cases.
key_novelty: The core idea is building a performance model that accounts for per-core memory traffic inhomogeneity—unequal memory access across cores—in shared memory systems.
contributions: Performance model for inhomogeneous memory traffic
Demonstrates inaccuracy of mainstream homogeneous-traffic assumptions
Improved time estimation for memory-bound applications
limitations: Abstract does not provide specific model accuracy metrics or experimental validation details; limited discussion of when inhomogeneity occurs
